ana: Heads-up — we have a puzzling perf delta between the synthetic streaming harness and the replay harness for small-chunk streams. Synthetic shows steady 3-6ms per-chunk while replay spikes to 20-60ms intermittently.

mike: Oof. Repro script + configs?

ana: Pasted quick commands I used:
```
# synthetic
./loadgen --mode=streaming --chunk-size=64 --qps=500 --seq-dist=short-tail
# replay
./replay_harness --streaming --preserve-timestamps --client-loop=burst --parallel=8 --chunk-handoff=true
```

sam: Did you pin the same kernel/quantization profile for both runs? Kernel selection can flip to generic for odd seq lengths.

ana: Good call. For synthetic I forced kernel=fast-attn-v2 but replay runs go through kernel-selector. Not pinned.

srini: That could explain it. Selector heuristics consider expected tail-length distribution + batching window. Replay's timestamp-aligned bursts create higher variance so selector falls back.

ana: I dug into profiling. When spikes happen we see:
```
# top of perf flame (condensed)
14% runtime:kv_cache::lookup_batch
11% runtime:client_readloop::drain
9% runtime:kernel_fallback_dispatch
7% kernel:matmul_generic
```

sam: kv_cache lookup batch up to 14% — interesting. Are chunk boundaries misaligned so we miss prefix cache?

ana: Exactly. Replay chunks often start in middle of previously cached prefixes because clients re-chunk differently, so cache hit rate drops 6->1%. That increases KV reads and causes readloop backpressure.

mike: Backpressure in client readloop leads to temporary queueing which pushes request sizes into an inefficient batching window. Kernel selector then sees a different sequence length histogram and chooses generic kernels. Cascade explains the spike.

srini: Steps to isolate: 1) force kernel pin on replay run 2) normalize chunking to align with cached prefix boundaries 3) add synthetic timestamp jitter to synthetic harness so it mimics replay burstiness.

ana: I ran 1 & 2. Forcing kernel removed the kernel_fallback_dispatch line and reduced tail p95 by ~30%, but KV misses still caused mid-tail spikes. Aligning chunking (client-side re-chunk to fixed offsets) reduced kv_cache misses and smoothed latency.

sam: Can you share the small test you used to normalize chunking?

ana: Here:
```json
{"client":{"rechunk_strategy":"fixed-offset","offset":0,"chunk_size":64}}
```

mike: Also try changing batching heuristic to prefer bounded-latency windows: set batch_max_wait=3ms, batch_max_size=32. If the harness creates bursts we want the runtime to avoid over-aggregating into pathological kernels.

ana: Will try. One more data point: perf trace shows occasional context-switch bursts when NV kernel allocation path hits contention. That cost is additive when KV reads already raised latency.

srini: That suggests two orthogonal mitigations: reduce KV miss rate + make kernel selection robust to bursty seq histograms. For the latter we should add a short smoothing window (ema) over seq histograms before selecting kernel.

sam: Related note — replay harness currently replays exactly-timestamped traffic which preserves client behavior. For apples-to-apples we should run: (a) replay-preserve-ts (b) replay-preserve-ts + client-normalize-chunking (c) synthetic-with-jitter + selector-pin, then compare.

ana: Agreed. I'll put up the runs on the dashboard. TL;DR: not a single bug — it's an emergent interaction: re-chunking -> KV miss -> readloop backpressure -> batching shift -> kernel fallback -> context-switch / alloc contention -> latency spike.

mike: Nice breakdown. Can you open a short RFC on a) adding a sticky kernel pin for debugging, b) smoothing histogram for selection, c) a small client-library change to prefer prefix-aligned chunks? We can triage which to prod-roll.

ana: Done — RFC draft up at https://rwd/internal/rfcs/streaming-chunk-alignment (putting notes there). I'll also attach the perf traces.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: kernel-pin debug image to canary cluster at 2026-03-18T15:10:00Z (image: runtime-debug:2026-03-18-kpin).

sam: Great. After the canary results we should run an apples-to-apples comparison and record the exact histogram inputs for selector tuning.

ana: Thanks all — I'll post results in this thread once canary completes. :thumbsup:
